item.title: Version 0.6.0
item.description:
Added

  • Greetings with an opinion. The dashboard greets you with a short, dry line about the day instead of a plain "Good morning": deadlines due today or this week, overdue work, classes left (or none at all), a kolokvijum or exam in the next few days, a grade you just entered, late nights, Mondays and Fridays, the exam period, holidays, and the start and end of the semester. In English or Serbian, following the app's language, and never the same line twice in a row. Settings ▸ General ▸ Funny greetings on the dashboard turns them off.
  • Open at login. Settings ▸ General ▸ Open Atelier at login, with the login item's real status, including when it still needs approval in System Settings.
  • Menu bar icon. Today's remaining classes and the next deadlines, one click from the menu bar, with Open Atelier, Settings… and Quit Atelier. Choosing a class opens its course, and a deadline opens Deadlines. Settings ▸ General ▸ Show Atelier in the menu bar hides it.

Changed

  • Atelier now remembers when points and exam results are entered, so the greeting can react to a fresh grade. Existing data is upgraded automatically; grades entered before this version have no date.

Fixed

  • A course's ECTS credits are typed like any other field (select, delete and replace digits) and line up with the rest of the course form; an empty field means 0 and numbers above 30 become 30.
  • Add Exams lists every course that isn't archived: courses not passed yet first, then passed courses (to retake an exam for a better grade), then the courses already in the period, shown ticked.

item.title: Version 0.5.0
item.description:
Fixed

  • Milestones can be deleted again: point at one and click the − button, or right-click it. The same button removes grade items.

Changed

  • Undo for deletions. Edit ▸ Undo (⌘Z) brings back a deleted assignment, note, file, class, milestone, grade item or exam, with its links to courses and projects. Deleting a single assignment, note or file no longer asks first; deleting a course, a project, an exam period or several assignments still asks, and can't be undone. Text fields keep their own undo while you type.
  • Edit sheets for assignments, notes, classes, exams and exam periods have a Delete button, and the Delete key removes the selected files or asks to delete the selected course.
  • Rows and cards highlight when you point at them, and more of them have a right-click menu (dashboard, course, project and grades pages). Archiving, pinning, deleting and the Show Completed and Show Archived filters animate.
  • A file tile is selected on the first click, without waiting to see whether it's a double click.
  • Double-click an empty part of a day in the timetable to add a class at that time.
  • In "New …" sheets, Cancel sits next to Add. The Deadlines filter is a menu, exam rows use a smaller status menu, and a new milestone's date is picked from a calendar button.
  • The Grades page keeps its three tiles in one row, and the Grades and Timetable pages show only their welcome message until there's something to show. Course tiles and project cards fill the width of the window.
  • The Scale Converter updates while you type and accepts a decimal comma (1,5).

item.title: Version 0.4.0
item.description:
Added

  • Exams. Add the exam periods (ispitni rokovi) you need, starting from typical dates for January, February, April, June, July, September or October, and choose which exams you'll take in each. Each period shows when registration opens and closes and how many exams aren't registered yet, with Mark All as Registered.
  • Reminders when registration opens, two days before it closes and on its last day, and before each exam (using the default reminder in Settings). Exam days and the end of registration appear in Deadlines, Up Next and the "Atelier" calendar, and exam periods show in the calendar as all-day spans.
  • An exam's date, room, points and grade can be entered. A passed exam's grade becomes the course's final grade and its points go into the course's exam. Each course's Grades tab lists its exams, and the dashboard shows the coming exam period from three weeks before registration opens.

Changed

  • The dashboard, course, project and grades pages lay out their cards in two balanced columns that fill the window, or one column on narrow windows, with no gaps beside short cards. Empty cards take less room, and the dashboard's tiles show classes today instead of the number of courses.

item.title: Version 0.3.0
item.description:
Added

  • Organizing files. Each file is recognized as a drawing, 3D model, image or render, PDF or document. The Files view filters by kind, status and tag, sorts by date added, date modified, name or kind, groups by kind, course or project, or status, and shows a grid or a list.
  • Select several files with ⌘-click, ⇧-click or ⌘A, press Space for Quick Look, and set their status (draft, final, submitted) or kind, add or remove tags, move them to another course or project, or remove them from Atelier, all at once. Get Info renames a file in Atelier and shows where it is, when it changed and how big it is.
  • Linked folders. A course or project can link a folder in Finder. Its files appear in Atelier, and files saved there later (an export from Rhino or ArchiCAD, say) appear as soon as you switch back to Atelier. Renamed files keep their tags, and a file removed from Atelier stays removed.

Fixed

  • In Serbian, the menus macOS adds (Edit, View, Window, Copy, Paste, Hide, Quit, Settings… and a text field's right-click menu) were in English. They are now translated too, as are "Never" under Settings ▸ Updates and the confirm buttons of the backup folder pickers.

item.title: Version 0.2.0
item.description:
Added

  • Backups (Settings ▸ Backups): once a day, if anything changed, Atelier saves a copy of your data to a folder you choose, such as one in iCloud Drive, and keeps the newest 14. Restoring a backup first saves a copy of your current data, then reopens Atelier with the restored data. The dashboard says when changes haven't been backed up for a week, and the "couldn't open its data" screen can restore a backup too.
  • A course's overview shows its points and grade, and the Grades overview shows the grade your points already reach before the final grade is entered.

Changed

  • Each grade item has a remove button and an exam button, instead of options hidden in a right-click menu.
  • Points save as you type and accept a decimal comma ("12,5") as well as a point.

Fixed

  • Settings ▸ Backups ▸ Choose… didn't open the folder picker.
  • In Serbian, the titles of the New and Edit sheets (New Course, Edit Project…), the Start and Final review dates, and one file error message were still in English.

item.title: Version 0.1.2
item.description:
Security

  • Atelier checks that it is still signed with the certificate it was published with, at launch and again shortly after. A copy that was modified to skip activation and then re-signed won't open.

item.title: Version 0.1.1
item.description:
Added

  • Help ▸ Send Feedback… (also in Settings ▸ General) opens a short form to report a problem, suggest an idea or ask a question, with room for screenshots. The app version, macOS version and the screen you were on are filled in for you; your courses, grades and notes are never sent.

Fixed

  • The Terminal installer stopped at its first step with "unbound variable" on macOS's built-in bash.

item.title: Version 0.1.0
item.description:
Added

  • Dashboard with greeting, current semester and teaching week, counts of what is due this week and overdue, an "Up Next" list, active projects with progress, course tiles, recent notes and files.
  • Courses with code, instructor, room, ECTS credits, academic year and semester, color and symbol. Courses can be reordered and archived, and each has tabs for its assignments, projects, notes and files.
  • Studio projects with a design-phase track (brief → submitted), milestones (rename inline and change dates from a popover), a final review date, linked assignments, notes and files.
  • Assignments in a sortable, searchable table with an inspector: type, status, priority, due date and course or project.
  • Deadlines agenda that groups assignments, milestones and project reviews into Overdue, Today, Tomorrow, This Week, Next Week and Later.
  • Reminders as local notifications before an assignment is due.
  • Notes in Markdown with a preview, pinning, search and links to courses and projects. A new note left empty is removed automatically, and the Delete key deletes the selected note.
  • File references to drawings, PDFs, images and models on disk. Add them by drag and drop or the file picker. Thumbnails, Quick Look, Open and Show in Finder are supported, and missing files can be relinked with "Locate…".
  • Scale Converter tool: real ↔ drawing sizes at common architectural scales, the most detailed scale that fits an ISO A0–A4 sheet, and a quick-reference table.
  • Due dates that refresh every minute, so "Tomorrow" becomes "Today" and late items turn red without reopening a screen.
  • File ▸ New Window (⌥⇧⌘N) for a second window with its own navigation.
  • New assignment, project, course and note sheets open with the cursor in the title field, so you can start typing right away.
  • Timetable of weekly lectures, exercises and studio sessions on a Monday–Friday grid. Clicking a class opens its course, each course lists its classes, and the dashboard shows today's (or the next day's) classes.
  • Grades: points for each kolokvijum, project and exam, what each grade from 6 to 10 still needs, the final grade, the average and ECTS earned, by semester. Each course has a Grades tab.
  • Calendar sync (Settings ▸ Calendar): an "Atelier" calendar with open deadlines and the weekly timetable until the end of teaching, which also appears on an iPhone through iCloud.
  • Serbian (Latin) translation, chosen in Settings ▸ General.
  • Automatic updates with Sparkle, verified with EdDSA signatures.
  • Free distribution: a signed DMG on GitHub Releases, a download page, and a one-line Terminal installer that checks the app's signing certificate.
  • Activation: Atelier opens only on Macs activated with a code issued for that Mac, delivered as a link or pasted. Settings shows the activation and this Mac's code.
